speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision with black spots in your right eye, I need to determine if this is an opportunistic infection like Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Can you tell me how long you have noticed these symptoms, and do you see any flashes of light or a "curtain" coming down over your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms are concerning for CMV retinitis given your AIDS history and the 2-day onset of floaters and vision loss. You mentioned fungal esophagitis and Kaposi's sarcoma in the past; have you been maintaining your current CD4 count, and are you currently on antiretroviral therapy? I will need to see a fundoscopic exam, so REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopy Right_Eye.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis. The clinical presentation of painless vision loss and floaters in an AIDS patient, confirmed by fundoscopy showing necrotizing retinitis, is classic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis. Immediate initiation of anti-CMV therapy (e.g., ganciclovir) and optimization of antiretroviral therapy are required.
